note: Motion words that make a prompt better, by category. Each term: what it means, a way to say it to the agent, and the demo the library guide plays for it (tools/library_guide.html, .demo[data-demo]). Easing names are the library's own curves.

terms.means: The same move starts on each layer a few frames after the last.
terms.say: Stagger the cards by 3 frames.

terms.means: The next move starts before the last one ends, so the motion flows.
terms.say: Let the title overlap the subtitle a little.

terms.means: A pause where nothing moves, so the eye can read.
terms.say: Hold the logo for a second before it leaves.

terms.means: A moment the motion lands on: a word, a hit in the music, a cut.
terms.say: Land every title on the beat.

terms.means: How long a move takes. The library's are Glide, Arrive, Sweep and Stage.
terms.say: Make the entrances Arrive, the exits Glide.

terms.means: A delay between two things on purpose, so they don't move as one block.
terms.say: Offset the icon from its label by 4 frames.

terms.means: Fast start, soft stop. The Land curve: things arriving.
terms.say: Bring it in on Land.

terms.means: Slow start, fast end. The Launch curve: things leaving.
terms.say: Send it out on Launch.

terms.means: It goes past its place and comes back. The Pop curve.
terms.say: Pop the badge in with a little overshoot.

terms.means: A small move back before the real one. The Wind-up curve.
terms.say: Add a wind-up before it slides.

terms.means: Almost all the change at once, then a tiny settle. Editorial cuts.
terms.say: Snap the shapes on the action.

terms.means: The same speed all the way. The Flat curve: for opacity and loops, rarely for moves.
terms.say: Keep the rotation linear.

terms.means: A shape flattens when it lands and stretches when it's fast. It feels alive.
terms.say: Give the bounce some squash and stretch.

terms.means: Parts keep moving a moment after the body stops.
terms.say: Let the antenna follow through.

terms.means: A very fast move with motion blur, like a camera snapping.
terms.say: Whip the next card in.

terms.means: Near layers move more than far ones: depth without 3D.
terms.say: Add parallax between the background and the type.

terms.means: A slow loop up and down, so a still thing looks alive.
terms.say: Let the icons float while the VO plays.

terms.means: A short jitter that dies out: an impact, a bass hit.
terms.say: Shake the frame on the hit.

terms.means: Each letter animates on its own, one after another.
terms.say: Bring the title in by character.

terms.means: Words rise from behind an invisible edge, as if cut from the line.
terms.say: Mask-reveal each line from below.

terms.means: The space between letters. Opening it slowly feels premium.
terms.say: Let the tracking settle in.

terms.means: Words hit the frame from big to their size, with a kick.
terms.say: Slam the three words in.

terms.means: Letters appear one at a time with a cursor.
terms.say: Type the line in with a cursor.

terms.means: Type that moves with the voice or the music, as the main show.
terms.say: Make this quote kinetic type on the VO.

terms.means: A quick zoom into the shot to make a moment hit harder.
terms.say: Punch in on her line.

terms.means: The clip speeds up, slows down for the moment, speeds up again.
terms.say: Ramp it: fast in, slow on the hit, fast out.

terms.means: The shot stops on one frame while graphics play over it.
terms.say: Freeze on her close-up and add the title.

terms.means: A graphic follows something moving in the shot.
terms.say: Track the car and pin a label to it.

terms.means: A cut-out of the people, so text can go behind them.
terms.say: Matte the two of them and put YES! behind.

terms.means: The camera flies into a word or a logo and through it.
terms.say: Push through the logo into the next scene.

terms.means: A shape or colour crosses the frame and carries the change.
terms.say: Join the scenes with a two-colour wipe.

terms.means: The cut happens in the middle of a move, so it feels invisible.
terms.say: Cut on the action, not after it.

terms.means: How much and how fast things move: 1 calm to 5 explosive.
terms.say: Keep the energy at 2, calm and soft.

terms.means: The feel words: modern, elegant, playful, editorial, technical, warm.
terms.say: Make it modern and a little playful.

terms.means: Space and pauses between moves, so nothing fights for the eye.
terms.say: Give it more breathing room between beats.

terms.means: Fewer, better moves. One hero move per scene.
terms.say: Only the title moves big; keep the rest quiet.

terms.means: Things travel on curves, the way a hand or a ball does, not on rails.
terms.say: Move the cursor on an arc, not a straight line.

terms.means: A small move that answers the main one: a ripple on a click, a float, a settle. Never louder than the hero.
terms.say: Add a ripple when it clicks.

terms.means: One idea per frame, so the eye knows where to look.
terms.say: Stage it: only the price comes forward, dim the rest.

terms.means: Design the end frames first, then the moves between them.
terms.say: Show me the end pose of each scene before you animate.

terms.means: Push the key move a little past real so it reads small, and stop before it turns theatrical.
terms.say: Push the pop a bit more, then settle.

terms.means: Timing tells how heavy a thing is: light things move fast and land soft, heavy ones take longer and settle.
terms.say: Make the card feel heavier: slower in, firmer landing.

terms.means: Letters flick through display faces and settle on the brand font, one after another.
terms.say: Swap fonts on the wordmark, then let it settle left to right.

terms.means: A named cursor that does the actions on screen: travels, clicks, drags, then leaves.
terms.say: Add Dana's cursor clicking the two cards.

terms.means: A selection box dragged open from a corner, with handles and the frame's size.
terms.say: Draw a selection around the hero card.

terms.means: Cuts and key moves land on the music's beats, found from the track itself.
terms.say: Put markers on the music's beats and cut on every second one.

terms.means: The music dips under the voice and comes back between lines.
terms.say: Duck the music 9 dB under the voice-over.

terms.means: The voice is timed first; every scene, cut and word follows its phrases.
terms.say: Lock the timing to the voice-over, then build the scenes.
